subsystems.name: Reservoir substrate
subsystems.role: a physical quantum system whose natural, untrained dynamics provide the memory and mixing.

subsystems.name: Input encoder
subsystems.role: injects the data stream by modulating the reservoir rather than by running gates.

subsystems.name: Evolution and control
subsystems.role: lets the system run under its own physics for a fixed, short time.

subsystems.name: Measurement stage
subsystems.role: turns the reservoir's final state into classical numbers.

subsystems.name: Classical readout layer
subsystems.role: the only trained part: a simple linear map from measured features to output.

subsystems.name: Benchmark harness
subsystems.role: proves the reservoir is actually useful rather than just interesting.
parts: classical baselines such as echo-state networks

buildSteps.title: Pick the task
buildSteps.detail: Choose a temporal problem — forecasting, classification or chaotic-system prediction — with a clear metric and a known classical baseline.

buildSteps.title: Choose a substrate
buildSteps.detail: Select a quantum system with rich, controllable internal dynamics: a superconducting qubit chain, a photonic interferometer with squeezed light, cold atoms or a spin ensemble.

buildSteps.title: Fix the dynamics
buildSteps.detail: Tune couplings, detunings and drive strengths once, then freeze them. Nothing inside the reservoir is ever trained.

buildSteps.title: Design the input encoding
buildSteps.detail: Map each time step of the data onto a physical knob — a rotation angle, field strength or drive amplitude — so successive inputs leave fading traces in the system.

buildSteps.title: Run the reservoir
buildSteps.detail: Let the system evolve for a short, fixed interval per input; the complexity of the output features comes from the many-body dynamics, not from applied gates.

buildSteps.title: Measure observables
buildSteps.detail: Read out short-time correlation functions or Pauli expectation values. Many repeated shots are averaged to beat down shot noise, since the reservoir is reinitialised or left running.

buildSteps.title: Train the readout
buildSteps.detail: Collect features into vectors and fit a linear model with ridge regularisation on labelled examples. This is cheap classical optimisation — no parameter-shift gradients, no barren plateaus.

buildSteps.title: Validate against classical reservoirs
buildSteps.detail: Test on held-out data and compare with an echo-state network of similar size. Only a win that survives this comparison counts.

buildSteps.title: Scale or embed
buildSteps.detail: Add qubits, moves to real-time measurement and feedback, or specialise the reservoir to a niche such as forecasting a quantum device's own behaviour.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum processors with controllable many-body dynamics
prerequisites.why: small arrays of superconducting qubits and photonic circuits exist, but large, well-characterised reservoirs do not yet run reliably.
some schemes need measured outputs fed back into the reservoir within microseconds.
the reservoir must forget old inputs gradually; too much decoherence erases the signal, too little loses the memory.

prerequisites.tech: Theory linking dynamics to task performance
prerequisites.why: there is no reliable way to predict which physical reservoir will beat a classical one on a given task.
the readout training is standard, mature data science.

pathway.milestone: small laboratory demonstrations on a few qubits and photonic circuits
pathway.unlocks: evidence that fixed quantum dynamics can supply useful features.

pathway.milestone: rigorous benchmarks against classical reservoirs on temporal tasks
pathway.unlocks: a clear picture of where, if anywhere, the quantum reservoir wins.

pathway.milestone: error-aware and real-time-feedback reservoirs on mid-scale hardware
pathway.unlocks: longer input sequences and online operation.

pathway.milestone: narrow practical deployment, such as classifying or forecasting data from quantum devices themselves
pathway.unlocks: a stepping stone toward broader quantum machine learning if advantage holds.
